column1: P1 Final Submission rev. FA26 b
column3: Does the app do what Project 01 required? TWO HARD GATES: local storage must be Room or SQLite on the device (not Firebase or a remote store), and the UI must be Kotlin Compose (not XML layouts). Missing either gate scores 0 on this row no matter how the app looks. The rest is judged on what the video actually shows working.
column6: Both gates met. Login shows data specific to that user, a real external REST API is consumed, and information persists across app restarts. Demonstrated in the video.
column9: Both gates met. Login, API and persistence all work but something is visibly incomplete or buggy.
column12: Both gates met. The API is consumed but persistence or user-specific login is incomplete.
column15: Both gates met but the core loop is missing: no real API, or no login.
column18: A gate is missed (XML layouts, or no local Room/SQLite storage), or the app does not run.

column1: P1 Final Submission rev. FA26 b
column3: The agile process this course has graded all term, and the heaviest-weighted team row in Project 01: issues closed through pull requests, work done on branches rather than main, reviews actually submitted before merges, and tests that exist and run. Process matters more than polish here; Projects 02 and 03 shift that balance.
column6: Issues are linked and closed by PRs, all work went through branches, PRs carry submitted reviews from teammates, and real tests exist and run.
column9: The process is visible but inconsistent: some direct-to-main commits, several merges with no submitted review, or tests that are thin or boilerplate.
column12: Branches and PRs were used, but issues were not closed through them and reviews are mostly absent.
column15: Work landed on main without pull requests, or there is no usable issue and review history.

column1: P1 Final Submission rev. FA26 b
column3: The video shows the app genuinely running (the same recording used for the presentation), and the README is good enough that someone who has never seen the repo could clone it, build it and run it.
column6: Video shows the working app end to end. README covers what the app does, how to build it, and how to run it.
column9: Either the video skips core functionality, or the README is missing build or run steps.
column12: No working video, or a README that would not get anyone running.

column1: P1 Final Submission rev. FA26 b
column3: Substantive pull requests across the WHOLE project that you authored. Authorship means the commits inside are yours: opening a pull request that contains a teammate's commits is not your contribution and does not count here.
column6: Several merged PRs carrying real feature work you wrote.
column9: Merged work exists but is thin, or is concentrated in one burst rather than across the project.
column12: Only config, formatting or one-line changes, or PRs whose commits were authored by teammates.
column15: No merged work of your own.

column1: P1 Final Submission rev. FA26 b
column3: GitHub issues assigned to you and closed by your own merged work across the project.
column6: Multiple issues assigned to you and closed by your PRs.
column9: At least one issue assigned to you and closed.
column12: No issues assigned to you, or none ever closed.

column1: P1 Final Submission rev. FA26 b
column3: Reviews you actually submitted on teammates' pull requests. Merging someone's PR without submitting a review is not a review.
column6: Submitted reviews on several teammates' PRs, with comments that engage the code.
column9: Submitted at least one real review.
column12: No submitted reviews, or only merges with no review attached.
